production_query.plan: SEARCH operation_items USING INDEX ix_operation_items_operation_id (operation_id=?); USE TEMP B-TREE FOR LAST TERM OF ORDER BY
production_query.problem: OR state filter prevents state index lookup; every selected operation's items are examined before the 201-row response cap can be applied. SELECT Operation and OperationItem also projects unused private JSON and text.

changes: split failed/not_executed and qualifying skipped states into UNION ALL
retain original operation_id/position sort, 201 failure witness, all output formatting and safe reason rules
candidate.plan: MERGE (UNION ALL); each branch SEARCH operation_items USING INDEX ix_items_progress (operation_id=? AND state=?); temporary sorting of matching states remains

warm_comparisons.fixture: mostly pending/succeeded; target padding 2048 bytes and operation parameters padding 65536 bytes

candidate_semantics.method: process-local function binding; production files remain unchanged

limitations: Timing is warm in-memory SQLite only, not a real disk/EXE throughput promise.
VM steps are sampled every 100 instructions, including result fetching; tiny variation up to a few hundred is instrumentation quantization.
The probe does not establish real target sizes, real page locality or real physical I/O; scanning all table records and unnecessary selected payloads are confirmed query defects.
Candidate still scans all matching failure/skipped states and sorts; huge failed/skipped history, huge Operation.result payloads, or many operations remain open budget cases.
Service-level read budgets, cancellation, deduplication and lifecycle protections are separate work; this candidate alone does not establish unified protection.
